innei-ryugi-artifacts.description: Use when seeing decides faster than reading — UI directions or mockups to choose between, a page to tune or click through, a design doc, review, proposal, or architecture walkthrough for them or their team to read — or when they ask for an artifact or artboard by name, or for a link to share one, or when they paste a Ryugi Cloud link (…/a/…) to read, including during brainstorming.

innei-ryugi-design-system.description: Use when a project without its own design system needs several screens or a whole UI designed, when its screens exist but its style values are scattered with no tokens, when only a product doc exists and the UI is about to be designed, or when your human partner asks to build, rebuild or refresh a design system, design tokens or a visual language.

innei-ryugi-executing-specs.description: Use when an approved spec or design document is ready to implement and your human partner chose inline execution, or when they point you at a written design and ask you to build it in this session

innei-ryugi-interface-craft.description: Use when a visible product interface needs design judgment, including UI mockups during brainstorming, landing and marketing pages, visual direction exploration, reviewing an existing screen, or refining a prototype that feels generic or inconsistent.

innei-ryugi-isolated-agent-eval.description: Use when an unattended agent session in a test could act on Ryugi Cloud — publish, auto-publish, or use a Cloud sign-in — including writing-skills baseline and with-skill runs and pressure scenarios that use artifacts with `--auto-approve`.

innei-ryugi-using-git-worktrees.description: Use when ryugi:executing-specs or ryugi:test-driven-development sends you here before the first implementation edit, when uncommitted work has to move to or be committed on a branch other than the one checked out, or when work done in a worktree has landed

innei-ryugi-using-ryugi.description: Use when starting any conversation - routes each task to the Ryugi workflow for its stage

innei-ryugi-verifying.description: Use before telling your human partner that work is done, fixed, live or ready, whatever it touched — UI, an API, a CLI, data, a deploy, performance — and before fixing a bug they can see, to capture it first
